Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

intervention noun

also intervene, interfere, interference, step in, get involved, veto (verb), interpose a veto, meddle

classical

Cic. Leg. 3.8: nisi mihi levissimus tribūnus plēbis intercessisset (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 181, 402

intercēdō, intercēdere, intercessī, intercessum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

intervene, step in between; of a tribune, veto

Literally to come or be between; so to intervene for or against someone, and in Roman politics to veto a measure. The noun is intercessiō (veto; intervention).

Other words

  • sē interpōnere — intervene, interfere, get involved

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 10.27.2: sī tē in istam pācificātiōnem nōn interpōnis (Lewis & Short); Cic. Q. fr. 3.4.5: mē nihil interpōnō; Traupman 334

    To put oneself into a matter, for good or ill; mē nihil interpōnō is “I’m staying out of it”.

  • interventus, interventūs m. — an intervention, a coming in

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.11.1 (Lewis & Short); Plin. Ep. 10.68 (Trajan): interventus prīncipis · Declension on Wiktionary

    Someone’s arrival or stepping in; also of things that come between (interventū noctis, Caes. BG 3.15).

Examples

  • Rixantur frātrēs; nōlō mē interpōnere.

    The brothers are squabbling; I don’t want to get involved.composed

See also don’t interrupt me!, help, prevent, argument.

SourcesLewis & Short: intercedo · Lewis & Short: interpono · Lewis & Short: interventus

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
